description: Given a circular sorted linked list, insert a new integer value into it such that it remains sorted. The list may have duplicate values. Return any node of the list.
intuition: In a sorted circular list, there are three insertion cases: the value fits between two nodes normally, it is the new max or min (insert at the wrap-around point), or all values are the same (insert anywhere). Traversing the list once handles all cases.
approach: Traverse the list to find the correct insertion point. Handle three cases: normal insertion between two nodes, insertion at the wrap-around point (max to min), and when all values are the same.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: head = [3→4→1→(back to 3)], insertVal = 2

Start: curr=node(3)

Iteration 1: curr=3, curr.next=4
  Case 1: 3 <= 2 <= 4? No (2 < 3)
  Case 2: curr.val(3) > curr.next.val(4)? No
  curr.next !== head → advance

Iteration 2: curr=4, curr.next=1
  Case 1: 4 <= 2 <= 1? No
  Case 2: curr.val(4) > curr.next.val(1)? YES → wrap-around!
    insertVal(2) >= curr.val(4)? No
    insertVal(2) <= curr.next.val(1)? No
  curr.next !== head → advance

Iteration 3: curr=1, curr.next=3
  Case 1: 1 <= 2 <= 3? YES → break!

Insert: newNode(2).next = node(3), node(1).next = newNode(2)
Result: [3→4→1→2→(back to 3)]
explanation:
1. Case 1: insertVal fits between curr and curr.next normally.
2. Case 2: At the wrap-around (max -> min), insertVal is >= max or <= min.
3. Case 3: All values are the same; insert anywhere (full loop detected).
4. Insert the new node after curr.
hints: Find where the new value fits in the sorted circular list.
Handle the wrap-around point specially (largest to smallest transition).
Handle the case where all values are the same.
